title: Finite-type ideal sheaves give finite-type module sheaves
statement: For any scheme X [def-pc-scheme] and ideal sheaf I [def-nagata-extended-ideal], if I.ofFiniteType then I.toModules is a sheaf of O_X-modules of finite type. No compactness, quasi-separatedness or separate quasicoherence hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Properties of Schemes, Lemma 28.23.3, Tag 01PG; Sheaves of Modules, Definition 17.9.1, Tag 01B4

proof.text: On each affine U choose a finite generating set t of I.ideal U. The range equality for toModulesι lifts each generator to a section of I.toModules. Restrict these sections to objects of Over U to form sections of I.toModules.over U and define the morphism π from the finite free sheaf by freeHomEquiv.

On any smaller affine V, map_ideal and Ideal.map_span show that the ideal is generated by the restricted t. The range of the composite toModulesι after π is a submodule containing those generators, by the freeSection identity. Hence it contains I.ideal V. The range equality and injectivity of toModulesι imply that π is surjective on V.

Affine subopens cover each object of Over U. Therefore the image sieve of every section for π is covering, by mem_over_iff, so π is locally surjective and an epimorphism. Package its finite generating sections on every affine U as LocalGeneratorsData using iSup_affineOpens_eq_top, and apply IsFiniteType.mk.

proof_origin.place: Expanded the affine generator and union arguments of Tags 01PG and 01B4 into complete Lean proofs.

mathlib_searches.query: A sheaf of ideals whose sections on affine opens are finitely generated is a finite type sheaf of modules
A finite type ideal sheaf is a finite type sheaf of modules and a directed union of ideal sheaves is their colimit
mathlib_searches.results: Found IdealSheafData.ofIdeals, ideal_sSup, ideal_iSup and SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType. None states either bridge for IdealSheafData.toModules.
Found IsFiniteType, its constructor and local generator projection, and the finite-presentation instance. Finite-type ideals need not be finitely presented.

The source library has toModulesOfLE and its inclusion identity in Curve.DivisorIdealSheaf. Mathlib has directed supremum membership and affine basis morphism extension, but no ideal-module bridge theorem.
